solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beautiful youth ultimately serving some old lawmaker

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word serving

parts.note: some, as in 'some people', means any
the Medes of the ancient Persian empire gave their name to the unalterable 'law of the Medes and Persians'

explanation.surface: An ancient lawgiver's handsome young servant, glimpsed at the end of his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: A MEDE is a member of the ancient people whose laws, with the Persians', were proverbially unchangeable.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ganymede was the Trojan prince of outstanding looks whom Zeus carried off to be cupbearer to the gods.

clue.text: Use of a covering for the ears?

indicators.note: something meant for the ears is heard, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a veil is a covering, typically for the face

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the purpose of earmuffs or headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the ears' signals a homophone: 'a veil' is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means benefit or use, as in 'to no avail'.

clue.text: Big church in Kerry most affected by change

indicators.note: letters affected by change are altered in order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Some major church in County Kerry has been hit hardest by reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected by change' signals an anagram of IN KERRY MOST; the Irish setting misleads, as the church is in England.
explanation.definitionFit: York Minster is the great Gothic cathedral of the northern English city of York, among the largest in Europe.

clue.text: With O'Neill briefly in charge, start to study selective breeding

indicators.note: briefly means the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Eugene O'Neill was the American playwright

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word study

explanation.surface: With the playwright put in charge, a programme of controlled breeding is to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the last letter of EUGENE, leaving EUGEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugenics is the discredited doctrine of improving a population by controlling which people reproduce.

clue.text: Friendly understanding altered niece, not surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: A family member has changed, and unsurprisingly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder: 'surprisingly' shuffles ALTERED NIECE NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 Anglo-French agreement; the phrase now means any friendly understanding between nations.

clue.text: Feeble dog on lead in former times

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it
lead in points to the leading letter of the word former

parts.note: lab is short for labrador, a breed of dog
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A weak dog kept on a leash in days of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' and 'dog' suggest a leash, but 'lead in' takes the first letter of 'former', and 'times' is BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby describes something limp and lacking firmness, figuratively weak or ineffective.

clue.text: Understand family's first party finishing early

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word family
finishing early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: an at-home is a party held in one's own house

explanation.surface: Working out which family was first to leave the party.
explanation.walkthrough: An AT-HOME is a reception given at one's house; 'finishing early' cuts it to ATHOM.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to get to the bottom of it, that is, to grasp it.

clue.text: Bearing of one who will succeed on radio?

indicators.note: words on radio are only heard, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: an heir is the person who will succeed to a title or estate

explanation.surface: A question about how an heir to the throne carries himself in a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' signals a homophone: HEIR is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a person's manner or bearing, as in an air of confidence.

clue.text: See island store coated in baked clay, mostly

indicators.note: coated in means surrounded by the outer pieces, so the shop goes inside
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a brick is a block of baked clay
a shop is a store

explanation.surface: Look at an island shop whose walls are covered in brick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is the definition; 'mostly' drops the last letter of the baked clay, and 'coated in' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese or seat of office, and so is a bishopric.

clue.text: Indian city besieged by extremely threatening rabble once

indicators.note: a city besieged by a force is surrounded by it, so it goes inside
extremely points to the two end letters of the word threatening

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An Indian city surrounded by a menacing mob in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes T and G, the ends of 'threatening', which surround AGRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagrag is an old word for the riff-raff or rabble, as in 'tag, rag and bobtail'.

clue.text: Teacher expresses disapproval about minerals

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
ores are minerals from which metals are extracted

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher clicks her tongue over a geology lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: The tongue-click goes in the plural ('expresses'), so its final S lands after the minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutoress is a female tutor, an old-fashioned word for a woman teacher.

clue.text: Stick around lake, being down in the dumps

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: to gum is to stick something with glue
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone stuck by a lake, feeling miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Glum and down in the dumps both describe a gloomy, dejected mood.

clue.text: Charlie's new earnings docked before work on river

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it
docked means cut short at the end, as a tail is docked

parts.note: income is earnings
the Po is Italy's longest river
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Charlie has his new pay cut before starting a job on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name but is the definition; 'docked' cuts the last letter of the earnings, and 'on' puts the work after the river in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charlie is a fool, and so is a nincompoop.

clue.text: Case left by chap having meal with union leader

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a man is a chap
tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the word union

explanation.surface: A suitcase abandoned by a man eating with a trade union boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling bag or trunk that opens into two halves.

clue.text: Hanger-on in farm building, one left inside

parts.note: a barn is a farm building

indicators.note: inside means the letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: Someone tagging along hides out in a barn, one left behind inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is ACE, the one in a pack of cards, with L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle clings to rocks and hulls, so the word is used for a person who clings on, a hanger-on.

clue.text: Asian lad travelling around posh part of Spain

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
travelling suggests the letters are on the move into a new order

parts.note: U means upper-class, the posh register of English

explanation.surface: A young man from Asia touring a smart region of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges ASIAN LAD, which goes around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is the autonomous region of southern Spain containing Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Underdone cheese dish with bit missing

indicators.note: missing means the word bit is absent from the dish's name

parts.note: Welsh rarebit is a dish of melted cheese on toast

explanation.surface: A cheese dish served with a piece left out and not fully cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh RAREBIT is cheese on toast; with BIT missing it leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare meat is cooked only lightly, so it is underdone.

clue.text: State of mountain-climbing artist entertaining request

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: The condition of a mountaineering painter who takes on a commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the mountain upward in this down clue; 'entertaining' has the artist hold the request.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is a state in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Time to go back and make improvements

indicators.note: to go back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: It's time to return and do things better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is TIDE, as in 'time and tide', read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise it, correcting and improving it.

clue.text: Ancient history chum distorted excessively

parts.note: something that is over is finished, ancient history

indicators.note: distorted means the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A pal's version of the past has been grossly exaggerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges CHUM; 'ancient history' means something finished and done with.
explanation.definitionFit: Overmuch means to too great a degree, which is what excessively means.

clue.text: Illuminated sign colonel finally installed in clubs, perhaps

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: clubs is an example of a suit in a pack of cards

indicators.note: finally applies to both sign and colonel, taking each word's last letter

explanation.surface: A lit-up sign at the club, with the colonel finally fitted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' covers both 'sign' and 'colonel', giving N and L, which go inside SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlit means lit by the sun, so illuminated.

clue.text: Go to Paris, carrying cycle for versatile sportsperson

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other piece within

parts.note: aller is French for to go
a round is a cycle, a recurring sequence

explanation.surface: Taking a bike on a trip to Paris, for an athlete of many talents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Paris' marks a French word, the infinitive 'to go'; 'carrying' puts the cycle inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder in cricket and other sports is good at several skills, such as batting and bowling.

clue.text: Dark blue Bible displayed in major city

indicators.note: displayed in means shown inside the other piece

parts.note: NY is New York
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A dark blue Bible on show in a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy is the deep blue colour of naval uniforms.

clue.text: Southern African grassland sometimes considered in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: felt means thought or considered, as in 'I felt it right'

explanation.surface: An African grassland that some people regard in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sometimes' hedges the homophone: in its Afrikaans pronunciation the word sounds like FELT.
explanation.definitionFit: The veld or veldt is the open grassland of southern Africa.

clue.text: Female murder victim to be buried in Scottish island shortly

indicators.note: to be buried in means placed deep inside the other piece
shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides
Abel, killed by his brother Cain, was the first murder victim in the Bible

explanation.surface: A woman's murder victim is to be interred on a Hebridean island, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims ISLAY to ISLA, which holds ABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a woman's name, so a female in crossword terms.

clue.text: Disallow fruit? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word is kept, its first half

parts.note: a banana is a fruit

explanation.surface: A ban on fruit? Absolutely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it means take half of BANANA.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to prohibit it, that is, to disallow it.

clue.text: It's like a carapace maybe, the poet said

indicators.note: said means it is the spoken sound of the name that matters

parts.note: Percy Bysshe Shelley was the English Romantic poet

explanation.surface: A poet comments on something resembling a tortoise's shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' signals a homophone of SHELLEY, the Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is a hard shell, so something resembling one is shelly.

clue.text: Seabird identified by woman in luxury car

indicators.note: in means the name goes inside the other piece

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a fast luxury car
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A seabird spotted by a woman in a fancy car.
explanation.definitionFit: The gannet is a large white seabird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Assess English girl worried about university

indicators.note: about means the two pieces wrap round the other

parts.note: Val is a girl's name
ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: An English girl is anxious about her university assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is the past tense of eat in the sense of nag, as in 'what's eating you?'; 'about' has girl and worry surround the university.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate something is to judge its worth, that is, to assess it.
